subject: Private deployment: network segmentation & SOC 2 intake
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Tom Keller <tom.keller@nexahealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 09 May 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment: network segmentation & SOC 2 intake

Tom — great to meet earlier. Quick recap + next steps from our discovery: 

What we heard from you:
- Primary goal: run customer-facing LLM inference inside NexaHealth VPC (HIPAA + SOC 2 constraints).
- Preference for network isolation with a small set of egress-controlled bastion hosts for model updates.
- Target production date: late Q3; compliance gate required (SOC 2 type II evidence + limited-data-processing agreement).

Immediate asks from Redwood to help scope private deployment:
1) Can you share your high-level network topology (VPCs/subnets/zones) or an architecture diagram — attached is a lightweight template (network-diagram-template.pdf) if helpful.
2) SOC 2 status: current Type I/II? expected audit window? We need the scope (in-scope systems) and any existing attestations.
3) GDPR/HIPAA: any specific DLP or retention requirements beyond standard BAAs?
4) Vendor security questionnaire: we'll send a short form to collect environment specifics and mapping to our controls — completing it speeds the intake.

Suggested next steps:
- You / security team: return the diagram + initial answers to the questionnaire (link below) by EOD next Thu (2028-05-16) if possible.
- Redwood: produce a draft isolation-zone proposal (three options: single VPC w/ strict subnet isolation; dual-VPC with transit gateway; fully air-gapped on-prem pattern) + list of SOC 2 artifacts we will request.
- Quick follow-up call (~30m) to review the diagram and questionnaire responses — propose Tue 2028-05-16 10:00am PT; let me know availability.

Links and attachments: Vendor questionnaire (https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSdVendorSQForm), network-diagram-template.pdf (attached).

Thanks — we want to keep this low friction and align on evidence early so your compliance team doesn't get surprised.

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0173
Redwood Inference

From: Tom Keller <tom.keller@nexahealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: NexaHealth Security <security@nexahealth.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 May 2028 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment: network segmentation & SOC 2 intake

Soojin — thanks for the recap and the template. Attaching our current diagram (Nexa_current_arch.vsdx) and a quick answers sheet (nexa_security_answers.xlsx) for the items you listed. High level answers: 

- SOC 2: We completed Type I in 2026; Type II in progress with a target report window Aug–Sep 2028. We can share interim controls evidence (policy docs, access reviews) earlier.
- HIPAA/GDPR: We are a US-based covered entity with a BAA in place. Retention policies are governed by clinical record rules; for model inference logs we'd prefer a 90-day retention window for debugging then aggregated-only for telemetry.
- Network: We currently run two primary VPCs (prod and restricted-services). Prod allows limited outbound to vendor endpoints via NAT; restricted-services VPC hosts our analytics pipelines behind a firewall.

Quick Q for you: what level of egress control do you require for model updates (inbound pull vs scheduled offline updates)? Also, is a vendor-hosted but VPC-peered model acceptable if we can lock down traffic and key management?

We can aim to have the diagram + questionnaire responses back by 2028-05-16. If you need anything quicker let me know.

— Tom
Tom Keller
Head of Cloud Security | NexaHealth
tom.keller@nexahealth.com | +1 (212) 555-4432

Attachments: Nexa_current_arch.vsdx (1.1MB), nexa_security_answers.xlsx (28KB)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Tom Keller <tom.keller@nexahealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 May 2028 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment: network segmentation & SOC 2 intake

Tom — appreciate the fast turnaround and the files. Quick answers inline and next actions below.

Inline:
- SOC 2 timing: good to know. Interim artifacts will help us map controls now and reduce rework post-report.
- Retention: 90 days for inference logs is reasonable; we'll propose configurable retention per environment in the draft.
- Egress for model updates: we support three patterns (ranked by security):
  1) Air-gapped/manual import (customer exports model artifacts to USB/secure transfer; Redwood validates and uploads into the customer VPC offline)
  2) Inbound pull over a restricted management channel from a Redwood-controlled endpoint with client certs and mutual TLS
  3) Vendor-hosted with VPC peering or PrivateLink and customer-managed KMS for encryption keys (acceptable if legal/ops sign off)

Action items (what Redwood will deliver):
- Draft: Isolation-zone diagram + recommended subnet/security group set for the three patterns above (deliverable: RX-4821-isolation-options.pdf) — owner: Dylan (due 2028-05-18).
- Controls map: list of SOC 2 artifacts we will request and suggested temporary evidence we can accept pre-Type II (policies, access lists, SOC 2 Type I report) — owner: Lauren (due 2028-05-17).
- Short vendor questionnaire: please ask your security team to complete the form we sent (link below). That feeds our controls map and speeds the intake.

Can you confirm: (A) who from NexaHealth will own completing the questionnaire (name/email), and (B) whether you prefer a call or a short working session with our engineer to walk the diagram on 2028-05-16?

Link to questionnaire: https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSdVendorSQForm
Redwood working links: https://redwood-share.example.com/diagrams/RX-4821-overview

Thanks — we want to keep things lightweight and pragmatic so your audit path is predictable.

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com

Attachments: (none)

Tom — thanks for the files. I'll put together the isolation options doc and a high-level deployment diagram (RX-4821-isolation-options.pdf) this week. One quick ask: what is your target compliance cutoff for gating go-live (must-have SOC 2 Type II vs. acceptable with scoped mitigations until Type II arrives)? That will change the approach we show.

If you prefer, we can do a 45-minute working session on 2028-05-16 to sketch the exact network flows — propose 10:00am PT.

— Dylan
